messages:

Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@healthbridge.ai>

Subject: Questions on private deploy DPA redline (keys & transfers)

Hi Michael / Karthik,

Attached is our latest redline to the DPA — HealthBridge_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf. Two urgent areas we need explicit language for before legal signs off:

1) Customer-managed keys (CMK): We need to confirm whether Redwood will ever hold escrowed copies of CMKs for private deployments (VPC / on-prem). If so, what triggers release and what legal authorities can request access?

2) Operator access & telemetry: We understand operator access windows for breakglass, but need a clear limit on what telemetry/metrics Redwood collects in private deployments and which subprocessors may process those traces (e.g., cloud partner logs).

3) Cross-border transfers: HealthBridge is subject to EU patient data rules; we need explicit guarantees around subprocessor geofencing and a mechanism to approve any transfer outside EU/US.

Can you confirm acceptable contract language or point us to a suggested clause set? If helpful, we can set a short call this week.

Thanks,
Laura Simmons
Head of Security & Privacy
HealthBridge Analytics

Attachments: HealthBridge_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf (PDF, 2 pages redline)

Subject: Re: Questions on private deploy DPA redline (keys & transfers)

Hi Laura — thanks for the redline and clear asks. Quick answers and next steps below; Irene and Karthik are looped for technical/legal wording.

Summary answers:
- CMK escrow: Redwood does not retain customer CMKs for standard private deployments. We offer an optional escrow service only when explicitly requested in the SOW and with documented legal authority matrix; escrow keys are held in an HSM with dual-control, and release requires signed attestation from an authorized customer PO plus a judicial/subpoena process defined in the agreement.

- Operator access & telemetry: For private VPCs we limit telemetry to health metrics (CPU, GPU memory, scheduler traces) and anonymized request rates; we do not log PII or full request payloads. Subprocessors that may see telemetry are our cloud provider (for hosted managed VPCs) and a managed-support partner in APAC (for on-prem hardware maintenance) — both listed in the subprocessor schedule.

- Cross-border transfers: We can add a clause to require customer approval for any transfer outside the contract-specified geography and to commit to onshore subprocessors for regulated datasets where commercially reasonable.

Attached: redwood-privdep-handshake-summary.pdf — a short one-page summary of our operational constraints and recommended DPA language. Proposed next step: legal-to-legal redline session (30 minutes) + a technical runbook annex for your ops team. Are you available Thursday 8/31 10am PT?

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Enterprise Sales (Redwood Inference)

Attachments: redwood-privdep-handshake-summary.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

Subject: Internal: proposed DPA language — CMK escrow & telemetry carveouts

Michael / Karthik — copying the external thread below for context. I drafted concise clause options to insert into the DPA and a short operational playbook we can attach as an annex. Key points:

1) CMK custody clause (proposed):
"Customer Keys and Escrow: Customer retains exclusive control of Customer Master Keys (CMKs). Redwood will not take custody of CMKs except where Customer elects the Escrow Service under a separate SOW. Escrow Service terms: keys are stored only in FIPS-140-2 Level 3 HSMs, dual-control release requires (a) a valid customer-signed release affidavit and (b) a court order where applicable. Redwood personnel never export private key material outside HSM envelopes."

2) Operator access window & auditability (proposed):
"Operator Access: Operator access to customer environments for remediation is strictly time-limited, requires prior ticketing and customer approval except in defined emergency scenarios, and is recorded with tamper-evident audit logs made available to Customer on request. Telemetry: Redwood's telemetry collected in private deployments is limited to non-content health metrics and rate counters; request payloads are not retained beyond transient in-memory buffers required for processing. Subprocessor list is attached to the DPA and requires 30-days' notice and customer approval for additions that would enable cross-border data flows."

3) Cross-border transfer language (proposed):
"Cross-border Transfers: Redwood will not transfer Customer Data outside the geographies explicitly approved in the Order Form without prior written consent from Customer. For transfers that are necessary due to infrastructure failure, Redwood will use contractual and technical safeguards, notify Customer within 48 hours, and provide remediation options (e.g., onshore failover)."

Operational annex highlights (we should add): procedural steps for breakglass, list of telemetry fields, subprocessor contact matrix, and an escalation path for legal hold.

If you want, I can convert these into tracked changes against HealthBridge_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf. For scheduling: I can join the Thursday 8/31 10am PT slot Michael proposed.
